anya: quick FYI — prototyping a 'granular token surge' mitigation for noisy tenants. thinking a short-window per-tenant surge score + soft-shed policy.
liam: tl;dr — what's different from current lease/admission work? 
anya: current leases are too coarse for sudden bursts that look abusive (spikes across many small keys). idea: track a moving 'surge_score' computed from token rate + burstiness + probe patterns, TTL 30s.
sophia: curious how we compute burstiness without huge state. can this be sampled? 
anya: yes — use per-tenant rolling counters with probabilistic sketch for keys. store agg counters in admission service (small footprint). sample heavy-hitter keys for inspection.
mike: how do we act on score? soft-shed first, then degrade model variant? 
anya: policy: surge_score > 0.7 => apply soft-probabilistic admission (p=0.6). >0.9 => reject 429 for non-critical routes. also prefer cheaper model variants + prefix caching.
zoe: can we expose header so downstream services and customers can see? `X-Redwood-Surge-Score`?
anya: yep. plan to include header and structured event to telemetry. example header:
```
X-Redwood-Surge-Score: 0.82
X-Redwood-Quota-Window: 30s
```
liam: telemetry + alerting is key. need to avoid noisy auto-oscillation (score flapping). add hysteresis and min-duration before actions.
sophia: what about probe detection? many attackers do low-rate distributed probes to evade score.
anya: detect high entropy across keys + rising gradients. if we see many low-rate keys with coordinated bursts -> escalate to 'coordinated-probe' tag and apply stricter backpressure.
mike: does this change API surface? any new config for customers? 
anya: config knobs: per-tenant sensitivity, custom allowed burst tokens, model-fallback list. default safe for self-serve, sales can tune for enterprise.
ops-bot: deploy-checklist: add admission integration, header plumbing in edge, sketch store migration, telemetry dashboards, canary release to 10% of traffic.
zoe: can we run a shadow run first (score computed but not enforced) for 48h? 
anya: yes planning shadow for 72h with synthetic probe tests. then canary 1% -> 10% -> 100% with rollback gates based on false positive rate.
liam: +1 on shadow. also add a regression test harness for fairness metrics (p50 token latency per-tenant, false-reject-rate).
sophia: i'll prototype sketch+counter merge strategy. mike can you own runbook for oncall? 
mike: yep I'll draft the runbook and rollback playbook.
anya: sweet. next steps: sophia prototype, ops-bot checklist, zoe dashboard mocks. sync tomorrow 10am. (react :thumbsup:)
